meta.title: Shramko SOG LOD Converter: PLY → Streamed SOG with LODs for SuperSplat, in your browser
meta.ogTitle: Shramko SOG LOD Converter — giant splat PLY → SuperSplat-ready Streamed SOG with real LODs
meta.description: Convert huge 3D Gaussian Splatting PLY files (hundreds of millions of splats, 10+ GB) into a SuperSplat-ready Streamed SOG .zip with real levels of detail and SOG compression — on your own GPU, in your browser. Nothing is uploaded, nothing to install.
nav.label: Main
hero.title: Giant splat PLY → SuperSplat-ready Streamed SOG with real LODs
hero.lead: This free tool turns a 3D Gaussian Splatting PLY of any size into a Streamed SOG archive with levels of detail (LOD) and SOG compression, ready to upload to superspl.at. It runs entirely in your browser on your own GPU and CPU: the file is never uploaded, and there is nothing to install.
hero.by: Made by Andrii Shramko — scans, drones, Gaussian splats
app.title: Converter
app.dropHint: The file stays on your computer — it is read locally, never sent anywhere.
app.planTitle: Levels of detail that will be built
app.presetNote: Defaults match what SuperSplat itself does: every level keeps half of the previous one until the coarsest holds at most 1 million splats, chunks of 512K splats / 16 m. You can start right away.
app.saveNote: You will be asked where to save the .zip. It is written straight to that file as it is built, so the PC needs free disk space of about 10% of the PLY size.
app.autoReport: If something fails, send an anonymous error report so it can be fixed (no file, no file name, no personal data).
app.keepOpen: Keep this tab open. Your computer will not go to sleep while it works.
set.ratioHelp: Fraction of splats each coarser level keeps. 0.5 = SuperSplat's halving.
set.minCoarsestHelp: No new level once a level holds this many splats or fewer. SuperSplat uses 1,000,000 so the first view fits even a phone's budget.
set.adaptive: Adaptive (better on skies, uses more memory)
set.decimatorHelp: How coarser levels are made: neighbouring splats are merged into one.
set.shHelp: View-dependent colour. Fewer bands = smaller archive. SuperSplat keeps them.
set.iterationsHelp: Only matters when SH bands > 0. More = cleaner colour, slower. Default 10.
set.webpHelp: Lossless WebP compression effort 0–9. Higher = slightly smaller, slower.
set.nanHelp: Recommended. Broken values would make the LOD writer stop.
set.chunkHelp: How the scene is cut into streamable pieces. SuperSplat uses 512 / 16 / 8. For very wide scenes a larger size means fewer, bigger chunks.
set.memoryHelp: Browsers allow about 16 GB per tab. Use at most half of your PC's RAM. Less RAM = more, smaller tiles and more reading passes — slower but safe.
set.tileHelp: The scene is processed in spatial tiles that fit in memory. Auto picks the size from the RAM setting.
set.gpuHelp: About 4× faster simplification. Turn off only if the GPU causes errors.
set.workersHelp: Parallel WebP/SOG encoders. Auto = up to 4.
how.title: How it works
how.s1: The PLY header is read in a split second. The tool plans the levels of detail the same way superspl.at does on its servers: each level keeps half of the previous one, until the coarsest holds at most 1 million splats — 10 levels for a 259-million-splat scan.
how.s2t: Cut the scene into tiles that fit
how.s2: A browser tab can hold about 16 GB, and no single array may exceed 2 GB. So the scene is split into spatial tiles sized to the RAM you allow; a few sequential passes over the file load the tiles. That is how hundreds of millions of splats fit in a tab.
how.s3t: Simplify and compress on your hardware
how.s3: For every tile, splat-transform (PlayCanvas, MIT) merges neighbouring splats to build each coarser level — on your GPU via WebGPU — and compresses every streaming chunk to SOG: quantised positions, rotations and colours in lossless WebP textures.
how.s4t: Write one archive, then check it
how.s4: All chunks stream into one ZIP64 archive on your disk with lod-meta.json at the root, exactly the layout superspl.at accepts. When it is done the tool reads the archive back and checks every level, chunk and file before it says so.
why.title: Why real LODs matter (and the mistake they fix)
why.p1: A Streamed SOG with a single level is just the full-detail scene cut into chunks: the viewer still has to fetch full detail everywhere it looks, and the first frame waits for it. With real levels, SuperSplat shows the coarsest level within seconds and streams finer levels only near the camera, staying inside its 1–4 million splat budget on any device.
why.p2: Many hand-made bundles have exactly that problem — split into chunks, but with one level, so there is nothing coarser to show. This converter always builds the whole level pyramid, and its final check refuses an archive with one level for any scene over 1 million splats.

limits.title: Limits and risks — read before a big run
limits.list:
• Use desktop Chrome or Edge. They can save straight to disk and use WebGPU. Firefox and Safari fall back to browser storage, which needs as much free space as the archive and then a download.
  • Big scenes take hours. Expect roughly 25–40 minutes per 100 million splats on a fast workstation with a modern GPU, much longer on a laptop or without GPU.
  • Keep the tab open. Closing it or a crash stops the conversion; it cannot resume yet.
  • Memory: a tab may use about 16 GB. If your PC has 16 GB or less, set “RAM to use” to 4–6 GB.
  • The archive is about 5–10% of the PLY size. superspl.at accepts up to 10 GB per upload; drop SH bands if a huge scene goes over.
  • Beta. If something breaks, the error is shown on the page; with your permission an anonymous report is sent so it can be fixed.
faq.title: Questions
faq.q1: How do I upload a PLY larger than 10 GB to SuperSplat?
faq.a1: superspl.at accepts at most 10 GB per upload. Convert the PLY here into a Streamed SOG .zip — usually 5–10% of the PLY size — and upload that .zip at superspl.at → Upload. The archive already contains the levels of detail, so SuperSplat publishes it as-is.
faq.q2: What is Streamed SOG (SSOG) and lod-meta.json?
faq.a2: Streamed SOG is PlayCanvas's streaming format for large Gaussian splat scenes: a lod-meta.json index with a spatial tree, plus many small SOG chunks (meta.json + WebP textures), each holding one level of detail of one region. The viewer downloads only the chunks and levels it needs.
faq.q3: Why does my Streamed SOG have no levels of detail?
faq.a3: Because it was built from a single PLY without decimated levels: splat-transform then writes one level, cut into chunks. Real LODs need the coarser levels to be generated (decimated) and tagged. This tool does that automatically; check “lodLevels” in lod-meta.json — it should be more than 1.
faq.a4: No. The file is read by your browser and processed on your computer. The server only delivers this page. If you allow it, an error report sends technical details (browser, GPU, settings, the error text) — never the file or its name.
faq.q5: Which browser and hardware do I need?
faq.a5: Desktop Chrome or Edge with WebGPU (any recent NVIDIA, AMD, Intel or Apple GPU). 16 GB of RAM or more is comfortable; with 8 GB set “RAM to use” to 4 GB. The tool works without a GPU too, about four times slower.
faq.q6: How long does it take, and how big is the result?
faq.a6: A rough guide is 25–40 minutes per 100 million splats on a workstation with a modern GPU. The archive is about 12 bytes per splat over all levels for scans without spherical harmonics — around 6 GB for 259 million splats.
faq.q7: How many LOD levels are created, and why?
faq.a7: Each level keeps half of the previous one until a level holds at most 1 million splats: 1 + ⌈log₂(N / 1M)⌉ levels — the same policy superspl.at uses when it builds LODs itself. The coarsest level fits the smallest viewer budget, so the first frame appears fast on phones and headsets too.
faq.q8: Can I use the archive outside SuperSplat?
faq.a8: Yes. It is a standard Streamed SOG: unzip it and load lod-meta.json with the PlayCanvas engine's Gaussian splat LOD streaming, or read it back with splat-transform.
faq.q9: Is it free and open source? Can I host it myself?
faq.a9: Yes — free, MIT-licensed, built on PlayCanvas splat-transform (MIT). The code and a Docker setup are on GitHub: AndriiShramko/shramko-sog-lod-converter.
agent.title: For your AI agent
agent.p: Working with an AI coding agent? Paste this so it knows how to prepare scans for SuperSplat.
agent.prompt:
Task: prepare a large 3D Gaussian Splatting PLY for superspl.at (limit 10 GB per upload).
Use https://sog.flyreelstudio.eu (runs in the browser, nothing uploaded) or the open-source repo https://github.com/AndriiShramko/shramko-sog-lod-converter.
Output: a Streamed SOG .zip with lod-meta.json at the root and real LOD levels (each level = half of the previous, until <= 1M splats).
Verify before upload: lodLevels > 1, counts decrease, every file in filenames exists (run tools/verify-zip.ts from the repo).
Then upload the .zip at https://superspl.at → Upload.

contact.p1: I'm Andrii Shramko — I scan whole cities and buildings as 3D Gaussian splats with drones and build tools around them. I made this converter because my own scans (250M+ splats) did not fit SuperSplat's upload and the existing tools didn't build real LODs.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.p1: Controller: Andrii Shramko, Bydgoszcz, Poland — zmei116@gmail.com. Your PLY files never leave your computer. The server stores only what you send on purpose: feedback and cooperation messages (with a contact if you give one) and, if you allow it, anonymous error reports (browser, GPU, settings, conversion stage, error text — no file, no file name).
privacy.p2: Page-use counters are kept without cookies and without IP addresses. Google Analytics is loaded only after you accept it in the banner. Messages and reports are kept for up to 12 months and are used only to reply and to fix the tool.
privacy.p3: You can ask for a copy or deletion of your data at any time: write to zmei116@gmail.com.

ui.planNote: {levels} levels, {total} splats in total. The coarsest level is shown first, finer ones stream in near the camera.
ui.oneLevel: This scene has at most {min} splats, so one level is enough.
ui.over10: The estimated archive ({size}) may exceed superspl.at's 10 GB limit. Consider fewer SH bands in Advanced settings.
ui.compat.noWorker: This browser cannot run the converter (no module workers). Please use desktop Chrome or Edge.
ui.compat.noGpu: WebGPU is not available here — the conversion will run on the CPU, about 4× slower. Desktop Chrome or Edge is recommended.
ui.compat.noSave: This browser cannot save straight to disk. The archive will be built in browser storage and then downloaded — it needs free space for the whole archive.
ui.compat.mobile: Phones and tablets do not have enough memory for big scenes. Please use a desktop computer.
ui.beatSlow: no update for {s} s — a long step without progress events; this is normal for big tiles
ui.cancelled: Conversion cancelled. The partial file was discarded.
ui.doneTitle: Done — your Streamed SOG is ready
ui.verifyOk: Checked: lod-meta.json at the root, {levels} levels, every chunk and texture present, splat counts match.
ui.uploadSteps: Open superspl.at, sign in, choose Upload, and drop this .zip. It is published with its levels of detail as built here.
ui.errReported: An anonymous error report was sent (number {id}). It will be looked at.
ui.errReportFail: The error report could not be sent right now.
ui.errHintMemory: This looks like the browser ran out of memory. Lower “RAM to use” in Advanced settings (e.g. to 4 GB), close other tabs and try again.
ui.errHintGpu: This looks like a GPU problem. Turn off “Use the GPU” in Advanced settings and try again.
ui.errHintInput: The file can't be converted as it is. See the message above.
ui.crash: The previous conversion stopped unexpectedly at “{stage}” ({ago}). This usually means the browser ran out of memory. Lower “RAM to use” in Advanced settings, close other tabs and try again.
ui.fbOk: Thank you! Your report number: {id}. Mention it if you write again.
ui.fbFail: Sending didn't work this time. Your text is still here — please try again in a moment.
ui.leadOk: Thank you — I'll reply to your email personally.
ui.saveCancelled: Saving was cancelled — choose where to save the .zip to start.
